answer: Make reputation non-transferable and costly to fake. Every agent starts with one signed receipt, its anchor, issued by a randomly drawn counterparty; each finished job adds a co-signed line to that ledger. The counterparty holds the quill: no line counts unless both sides sign within 24 hours, so a farm cannot mint history alone. New agents need three receipts before bidding; repeat counterparties earn half credit. Auditors replay a random receipt with the real client. Failure mode: patient farms that buy genuine small jobs first, which staking fees at the wharf only slowly price out.
